findings.description: Exact column headers for both bands are pure code constants invisible in SHEET-TAB-004's text: accrual band = TAX_HEADER [Sale ID, Lot ID, Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Amount, Lifecycle State] (6 cols); reserve band = TAX_RESERVE_HEADER [Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall] (7 cols), asserted verbatim in tabs.rs. All 3 B-runs reconstruct these headers essentially verbatim. All 3 A-runs, working from spec text alone, each invent a DIFFERENT header set (none matches the real headers) -- the 3-way A disagreement corroborates that column schema is genuinely absent from SHEET-TAB-004 text and is a pure code-side pin (though it may properly belong to the cross-referenced SHEET-TAB-001 rather than being a true 004 gap).

Physical separation is implemented as two entirely independent named ViewTab objects (TAX_TAB = "Tax", TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary"), each published independently via batch_update_view with its own frozen header and its own DATA_START_ROW=2 anchor; there is no shared row-coordinate space and no gap arithmetic anywhere in lib.rs. Spec text only says 'physically separated,' pinning nothing about mechanism. All 3 A-runs unanimously invent a materially different mechanism instead: a single shared tab with a fixed blank-row buffer (BAND_GAP_ROWS/GAP_ROWS = 2) and a computed offset (summary_start = accrual_end + gap). Per the rubric this unanimous-but-untraceable A behavior is an assumption artifact, not a standalone A-finding, but it is the largest structural divergence between all three A-sketches and the real architecture.

Every Tax-tab cell (accrual and reserve-summary alike, including Tax Year and Amount) is a plain formatted Cell::Value(String) -- never Cell::Formula; no GOOGLEFINANCE-dependent live cell ever appears on this tab. SHEET-TAB-004 text says nothing about the value/formula split. Unanimous across B1-B3.

Amount renders as the empty string (never "0.00", never omitted) specifically when applied_cents is None; the five reserve-summary monetary columns are unconditional (AnnualRow's cents fields are non-Optional) and are the kernel's exact values with no re-derivation. Spec text is silent on this. Unanimous across B1-B3; correspondingly none of A1/A2/A3 modeled applied_cents as Optional at all (all three used a bare Cents/i64 field) -- wholly invisible from the spec-alone side.

Row order in both bands is exactly caller/kernel input order -- no sort, no reorder (plain iteration over the input slices). Spec text says nothing about ordering. Unanimous across B1-B3, and directly contradicts A1's explicit sort_by_key on (jurisdiction, tax_year, date) for both bands and A3's implicit BTreeMap-grouped reordering (only A2 preserves input order) -- the 2-of-3 A split on invented sort behavior further corroborates that ordering is genuinely spec-unstated.

TAX_RESERVE_TAB is deliberately excluded from VIEW_TABS (exactly 4 entries: Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax) and from workbook_tab_order()'s enumerated list -- documented as part of the Tax surface, not a fifth entry in VIEW_TABS, i.e. not a navigable top-level tab. Spec text never states this. Only 1 of 3 B-runs (B3) captures it explicitly; B1/B2 omit it entirely -- a real coverage gap within the B-direction's otherwise strong agreement.

A3 is the outlier among the A-runs: it derives the reserve-summary band by summing accrued_cents internally via a BTreeMap rollup, rather than accepting a separate kernel-precomputed AnnualRow/ReserveSummaryRow list as A1 and A2 both do (matching the real annual_rows parameter). This violates the stated crate boundary (sheets-view owns no accounting or tax math) and is a real 2-vs-1 architectural split in how the A-runs shape the function signature -- an A-direction stability issue rather than a spec-vs-code gap, but material to how much to trust A-side consensus.

notes: Ground truth read directly from crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (render_tax, TaxView, TAX_HEADER, TAX_RESERVE_HEADER, TAX_RESERVE_TAB, VIEW_TABS, workbook_tab_order) and tests/tabs.rs. SHEET-TAB-004's literal text is fully satisfied by the real code on every clause it actually states. No A-run surfaced a requirement traceable to the spec's own text that the code fails to honor; every A-vs-code difference found is self-flagged by the A-authors as an assumption with no spec-text basis, so per the rubric these are assumption artifacts, not findings. Meanwhile the code+tests pin substantial concrete behavior that SHEET-TAB-004's text never states, reconstructed with high fidelity by the B-direction. Caveat: some B-only items (headers, value/formula boundary) may be properly owned by the cross-referenced SHEET-TAB-001 rather than unique to 004.
